title: Quantitative characterization of the urine and serum metabolomes of children is essential for 'omics' studies.
ehr_evidence: Lau et al. have compiled robust, translatable quantitative metabolomics data on urine and serum samples for European children across six study locations.
summary: Commentary discussing the establishment of a quantitative reference metabolome for children using urine and serum samples from the HELIX birth cohort project.
key_findings: Metabolites were associated with body mass index, diet, and demographics.
Novel association found between urinary 4-deoxyerythronic acid and body mass index.
population: European children across six longitudinal birth cohort study locations
exposure_domain: Early-life exposome (diet, demographics, geography, socioeconomic status, pollutants)
limitations: Commentary format rather than primary research
Metabolome characterization limited to targeted kit and not fully comprehensive
Historical lack of pediatric metabolomic reference profiles
